G M E N T*

This judgment is emerged consequent upon the petition filed by the petitioners U/S 166 of M.V.
Act, claiming compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- on account of the death of G.Ravi, Son of Gangaiah in a road traffic accident.

*FACTS OF THE CASE IN NUTSHELL *
 2.

Facts leading to the case of the petitioners forthcoming in the petition that, on the fateful day of 18.5.2023 at about 10.00 a.m., G.Ravi was riding his Moped bearing No.KA-04-JG-9230, from Harokyathanahalli towards Doddabele, at that time,
 3 SCCH-18 MVC 3371/2023 KSRTC bus bearing registration No.KA-19-F-3355 came from behind, drove the same, with high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the moped.
As a result, deceased fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

3. Immediately, he was shifted to Government Hospital, Nelamangala, again he was to NIMHANS,
Bengaluru, while shifting to the hospital, he had died.
Thereafter, post mortem was conducted and the dead body was handed over to the petitioners.
Subsequently, obsequies and funeral ceremonies of the deceased was performed by spending Rs.3,00,000/-.

2  4.

It is further stated in the petition that, prior to the accident, the deceased was hale and healthy,
and was aged about 49 years.
Further, stated that, he was doing agriculture and was getting an income of Rs.30,000/- per month.
and he was contributing his entire earnings for the maintenance  4 SCCH-18 MVC 3371/2023 of his family, being the sole bread earner of the family.

Due to the unnatural death of the deceased,
the petitioners' life become dark, miserable and depressed and put to great financial hardship.
5. It is alleged in the petition that, the accident was occurred, due to the negligent act of the driver of the offending vehicle, KSRTC Bus bearing registration No.KA-19-F-3355.

In this regard, criminal case was registered against him, in Crime No.212/2023 for the offences punishable under section 279, 337 & 304(A) of IPC, on the basis of the first information, received in this regard.
As such, the respondent is liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
Hence, the petitioners have approached this court, seeking compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- consequent upon the death of G.Ravi in the alleged accident.

3  6.

After service of the notice of this petition,
the respondent had appeared through its counsel and filed the written statement, in answer to the case of the petitioners.
7. The respondent in the written statement has not seriously disputed the accident, and the death of G.Ravi.

It is contended that, on the date of the accident, the driver of the bus, drove the same slowly, carefully and cautiously at that time deceased was moving on the same route and without wearing helmet and due to over speed lost his control over the vehicle and dashed against the bus.

Further, contended that, the compensation claimed by the petitioners is highly excessive,
exorbitant and exaggerated.
With all these main grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition, against the respondent.

8. On the basis of the rival pleadings of both the parties, for final determination of this case, my  6 SCCH-18 MVC 3371/2023 predecessor in office had framed the following issues:
 *ISSUES*
 1) Whether the petitioners prove  that, G.Ravi, had died due to the  injuries sustained by him in a motor  vehicle accident that was taken  place on 18.5.2023 at about 10.00 Bhagya vs K.S.R.T.C on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99382697/
4  a.m. on Doddaballapura-Dabaspet  road, near JASS Toll, Huralihalli  cross, Bengaluru-Tumkur NH-48  road, Nelamangala, Bengaluru due  to the rash and negligent driving of  the driver of the KSRTC bus bearing  registration No.KA-19-F-3355 in an  actionable negligence?
2) Whether the petitioners are  entitled for compensation as prayed  for?
If so, at what rate?
From  whom?
3) What order or award?

9. In order to substantiate the case of the petitioners, petitioner No.1 by name Smt.Bhagya,
 7 SCCH-18 MVC 3371/2023 stepped in to witness box, and placed her affidavit evidence, in lieu of examination-in-chief, who was examined as PW1 in the case on hand.
At the time of her evidence, 17 documentary evidence got marked as Ex.P1 to Ex.P17.
10. On the other hand, to prove the defenses of the respondent has examined its driver of the offending vehicle, by name Bapu Gowda as RW1.

At the time of his evidence, placed 5 documents,
which were marked as Ex.R1 to Ex.R5.
After completion of the stage of the evidence, matter was set down for arguments.
11. Heard the arguments of both the counsel and perused the records available on record.

12. On appreciation of the evidence placed by the petitioners, I proceed to give my findings on the Bhagya vs K.S.R.T.C on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99382697/
5
aforesaid issues as follows:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative.

As per final order,
 For the following:
 R E A S O N S  ISSUE NO.1:
 13. It is the specific case of the petitioners that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle KSRTC bus bearing registration No.KA-19-F-3355, alleged accident had taken place.
Consequently, husband of the petitioner No.1, father of the petitioner No.2 by name G.Ravi. had died.
As such, the petitioners being the legal heirs of the deceased, have filed the claim petition for consideration.

14. On the other hand, the respondent though not disputed the accident and the death of G.Ravi,
strongly denied the allegations of the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle contending that, due to the mistake on the part of the rider of the two wheeler bearing  9 SCCH-18 MVC 3371/2023 registration No.KA-04-JG-9230 alleged accident had taken place, as the rider was riding the said vehicle without control and dashed against the right Bhagya vs K.S.R.T.C on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99382697/
6 handle of the two wheeler against the left side center of the vehicle of the deceased G.Ravi and lost control, consequently, the deceased fell down on the right side of the road.
In the said accident pillion rider by name Bhagya also, had sustained minor injuries and the deceased Ravi due to the grievous injuries, had died while taking treatment in the hospital.
As such, the rider of the two wheeler was sole responsible for the accident and its consequences.

15. On going through the above issue, burden is on the petitioner to prove the same, by placing cogent and convincing evidence in order to find out the truth in connection with the rival contentions of both the parties with respect to the above fact in issue.

Firstly, the petitioners herein, to prove their  10 SCCH-18 MVC 3371/2023 relationship with the deceased, had placed Ex.P14 to Ex.P16 Aadhar cards along with the D.L. of the deceased Ravui as per Ex.P17.
The recitals of the said public documents clearly evident about the relationship between the petitioner and the deceased.
The said relationship, is not seriously disputed by the other side  16.

Another crucial point to be discussed herein, about the proof of the negligence on the part Bhagya vs K.S.R.T.C on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99382697/
7 of the driver of the offending vehicle as per the allegations of the petitioners.

Among the police documents, on going through the Ex.P1 first information report speaks that the alleged accident had taken place on 18.5.2023, on the same day,
first information was given by one Arun Kumar said to have an eye witness to the accident.

On the basis of his first information, criminal law set in motion against the driver of the KSRTC bus bearing registration No.KA-19-F-3355 alleging that, he had  11 SCCH-18 MVC 3371/2023 committed the offences punishable under section 279 and 337 of IPC.
There is no delay in giving first information about the accident.

In the recitals of Ex.P2, the complainant has clearly narrated that,
offending vehicle was coming from the back side of the defending vehicle and dashed to the two wheeler of the deceased, consequently, Ravi had succumbed to the injuries and pillion rider of the defending vehicle by name Bhagyamma also, sustained injuries in the accident.
The material documents which laid down the case against the driver of the offending vehicle, remained unquestioned and unchallenged well within time, before the competent court of law.

17. Added to this, spot mahazar said to have Bhagya vs K.S.R.T.C on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99382697/
8 executed on the same day of execution of Ex.P1 and vehicle seizure mahazar also executed on the same day in the presence of panch witnesses, as well as the spot sketch, executed by the investigation officer  12 SCCH-18 MVC 3371/2023 as per Ex.P5 clearly evident about the involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident.

The said material document clearly evident about the negligence on the part of the driver of the bus,
alleged accident had taken place.
Since the death of G. Ravi is not disputed point in issue.
More discussion on inquest mahazar and PM report marked at Ex.P6 & Ex.P7 is not required.
But the said documents clearly speak that, on the history of RTA, G.Ravi had succumbed to the injuries.

18. Along with the aforesaid documents, police notices and reply to the police notices marked at Ex.P8 to Ex.P11, clearly evident about by involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident and name of the driver of the offending vehicle as well as the number of the vehicle.

Another material document, report of the IMV inspector Ex.P12 reveals that, after inspection of vehicles in question it was opined that, the cause of accident was not  13 SCCH-18 MVC 3371/2023 due to any mechanical defects of both offending and Bhagya vs K.S.R.T.C on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99382697/
9 defending vehicles.
The damages noted in the column No.5 of the Ex.P12, remained unshaken.
The said damages reflect about the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle to cause accident and its consequence.

19 . Ultimately, on going through the final report submitted by the investigation officer as per Ex.P13, on the allegations forthcoming in column No.17 of the final report reveals that, against the driver Bapu Gowda Halli, case has been registered alleging that, he had committed the offences punishable under section 279, 337 and 304(A) of IPC.
This final report remained unquestioned by the other side.

Though the police papers are not substantive piece of evidence, to consider the claim petition in the absence of contrary materials to impeach the said documents, there is no hurdle to  14 SCCH-18 MVC 3371/2023 consider the said document as conclusive proof in support of the above fact in issue.
20. On the other hand, to prove the defenses of the respondent authority, relied on the evidence of the driver of the offending vehicle by name Babu gowda.

As per the evidence of this witness, alleged accident had taken place due to the negligence on the part of the driver of the two wheeler as noted Bhagya vs K.S.R.T.C on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99382697/
10 above.

But, to prove his innocence, and to discard all the allegations made against him in the police papers, except the production of his statement,
requisition, I.D. card and DL, as per Ex.R1 to Ex.R5,
no other material documents were placed for consideration and to disbelieve the contents of the charge sheet submitted by the investigation officer.
Ex.R1 and its recitals, will not helpful

to impeach the police papers in toto, since the driver of the offending vehicle has not made an effort to file counter complaint, well in time before the competent  15 SCCH-18 MVC 3371/2023 police station and also before competent court of law

. In the Ex.R1, there is no proper whisper,
actually when the said statement was given by the driver of the offending vehicle.

21 . At the time of cross-examination of PW1,
though the learned counsel for the respondent put several questions and suggestions to prove the innocence of the driver of the offending vehicle,
nothing has been elicited to disprove the case of the prosecution, which was laid down on the basis of first information given as per Ex.P2.

On the other hand, at the time of cross-examination of RW1, not denied the suggestion that, final report has been filed against him, but he denied the institution of Bhagya vs K.S.R.T.C on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99382697/
11 criminal case against him.
Further, he has not denied about seizure of the bus in connection with the accident.

Further he admitted about the fact that, he has not challenged the charge sheet submitted against the investigation officer, but failed  16 SCCH-18 MVC 3371/2023 to place copy of the complaint, said to have given by him, as per his answer and to substantiate the same.
 22.

Over all appreciation of the evidence placed by both the parties in toto, I am of the view that, the petitioners have placed satisfactory evidence to prove the above issue, which remained unshaken by the other side.

Further, there is no cogent evidence from the side of the respondent, to show that, due to the sole negligence on the part of the rider of the two wheeler accident in question and its consequence were taken.
Hence, the evidence of the petitioners, prevails over the evidence of the respondent.
23. In the light of my detailed discussion held above, I am of the view that, the petitioners have placed satisfactory evidence to prove the above issue, which remained unshaken by the other side.

As such, without making much discussion on the  17 SCCH-18 MVC 3371/2023 Bhagya vs K.S.R.T.C on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99382697/
12 point of rash and negligent driving, I hold that, the accident was occurred purely on the part of the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle KSRTC bus bearing registration No.KA-19-F- 3355.

As such, the petitioners being the legal heirs and the dependants of the deceased, filed this claim petition.
Accordingly, I am of the view that, the petitioners have placed satisfactory materials on record, to prove the aforesaid issue.
Resultantly, I am answering the Issue No.1 is in the Affirmative.

ISSUE No.2:
 24.

Now coming to the point of quantum of compensation for which, the petitioners are entitled is concerned, every legal representative who suffers on account of the death of a person, due to a motor vehicle accident, should have remedy for realization of compensation.
Since in the death case, the legal heirs are the claimants.
In the case on hand, the  18 SCCH-18 MVC 3371/2023 relationship of deceased with the petitioners is not in dispute.
The petitioners have placed Aadhar cards, as per Ex.P14 to Ex.P16.
Other side, has not disputed the relationship and no contra materials available on record, to disbelieve the same.

Bhagya vs K.S.R.T.C on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99382697/
13  25.

Another aspect to be considered herein that, on going through the age particulars of the petitioners, mentioned in the cause title of the petition, reflected that, the petitioner No.1, in her young age, lost her husband, the petitioner No.2 in her early age lost her father.

On the other hand, the respondent herein, has not produced documents on record, to show the independent economic status of the petitioners, and to disprove their dependency,
with the deceased, during his life time.

By taking into consideration of all these factors, along with the evidence of PW1, it is crystal clear that, the petitioners were the dependents to the deceased during his lifetime.
 19 SCCH-18 MVC 3371/2023  26.

Another point to be discussed herein that,
to substantiate the case of the petitioners herein,
and to prove the actual age of the deceased, as on the date of the accident, petitioners have produced Aadhar card & driving license of the deceased, as per Ex.P14 & Ex.P17.
On going through same, the date of birth of the deceased, has been mentioned as 20.6.1973
The accident occurred on 18.5.2023.
If the said document is taken into consideration, as on the date of the accident, deceased G.Ravi, was aged about 50 years.

The said document, remained Bhagya vs K.S.R.T.C on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99382697/
14 unquestioned by the other side.
Hence I am of the view that, as on the date of the accident, the deceased was aged about 50 years.

For his age,
multiplier '13' is applicable as per the ratio in "Sarala Verma" Case.

27 . In connection with the work of the deceased, is concerned, in the main petition and  20 SCCH-18 MVC 3371/2023 also in the evidence of PW1, stated that, he was doing agriculture and getting an income of Rs.30,000/- per month.
But in support of definite income of the deceased, there is no iota of documents to show that, the deceased was earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
In such a situation, as per law, notional income has to be taken into consideration.
Hence, the income of the deceased is apt to be taken as Rs.15,500/- p.m., which will meet the ends of justice.
28. Another point to be taken in to consideration herein that, as per the petition, two persons were depending on the earnings of the deceased.
In this regard, about the deduction of the personal and living expenses is concerned, the principle laid down by the Honourable Supreme Court in, Sarala Verma Case at para No.14 is to be considered.

21 SCCH-18 MVC 3371/2023 Bhagya vs K.S.R.T.C on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99382697/
15  29.

Apart from this, it is also relevant to discuss, that the Honourable Supreme Court in the decision reported in,
 2018 SAR (Civil) 81.

National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and others,
 " It was observed that, "While determining the  income, an addition of 50 per cent of actual salary  to the income of the deceased towards future  prospects, where the deceased had a permanent  job and was below the age of 40 years, should be  made.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The addition should be 30 per cent, if the  age of the deceased was between 40 and 50 years.
In case the deceased was between the age of 50  and 60 years, the addition should be 15 per cent.
Actual salary should be read as actual salary less  tax.
In case the deceased was self-employed or on  a fixed salary
, an addition of 40 per cent of the  established income should be the warrant where  the deceased was below the age of 40 year.
An  addition of 25 per cent where the deceased was  between the age of 40 to 50 years.
An addition of  25 per cent where the deceased was between the  age of 40 and 50 years and 10 per cent where the  deceased was between the age of 50-60 years
should be regarded as the necessary method of  computation.
The established income means the  income minus the tax component.

Having considered the above, as per law laid down in the above case, in connection with the deduction of personal and living expenses is concerned, it is settled that, "where the deceased was  22 SCCH-18 MVC 3371/2023 married, the deduction towards personal and living expenses of the deceased should be one third (1/3rd) where the number of dependent family members is 2 to 3, 1/4th where the number of Bhagya vs K.S.R.T.C on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99382697/
16 dependent family member is 4 to 6 and one fifth (1/5th ) where the number of the dependant family members exceeds six."
In the light of the above proposition, in the case on hand, 1/3rd has to be deducted towards personal and living expenses out of the total compensation.
In the present case, deceased was aged about 50 years, as on the date of the accident.
For this age multiplier "13" is applicable.
Therefore, by considering the earning of the deceased as Rs.15,500/- per month and Rs.1,86,000/- per year.

If 25% future prospects is to be taken into consideration, then it comes to Rs.2,32,500/-
(Rs.1,86,000 +Rs.46,500).
Further, 1/3rd has to be deducted towards personal and living expenses in the income of the deceased.
Thus, net loss income comes to Rs.1,55,000/- (Rs.2,32,500-  23 SCCH-18 MVC 3371/2023 Rs.77,500).
This income has to be multiplied by multiplier "13".

Which comes to Rs.20,15,000/- .
 31.

Apart from this aspect, in connection with the loss of estate, consortium, and with respect to the funeral expenses, to calculate the quantum of the compensation under the aforesaid heads, it is relevant to note herein the following authority,
 2018 SAR (Civil) 81. National Insurance Company Limited.
V/ s Pranay Sethi and others,

Bhagya vs K.S.R.T.C on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99382697/

The Hon'ble Apex Court discussed various  aspects in connection with the claim petition  filed by the claimants for compensation.

And  also observed that while determining the claim  petition, the reasonable figures on conventional  heads, viz., loss of estate, loss of consortium and  funeral expenses should be Rs.15,000/-,
 Rs.40,000/- and Rs.15,000/- respectively.
The  aforesaid amount should be enhanced at the rate  of 10% in every three years.

32. In the light of the proposition laid down in the aforesaid case, I am of the view that, In addition to this, the petitioner No.1 being the wife of the deceased, the petitioner No.2 & 3 being the  24 SCCH-18 MVC 3371/2023 children of the deceased, are entitled for sum of Rs.40,000/- in the head of loss of consortium.
Further, the petitioners are also entitled for sum of Rs.15,000/- towards funeral expenses.
And also the petitioners are entitled for sum of Rs.15,000/- in the head of loss to the estate.
Further the petitioners are entitled for Rs.10,000/- towards transportation of dead body.

Apart from this, it is to be noted that, in Pranay Sethi's case, the Honourable Apex court,
observed that, after expiry of every three years, from the date of judgment, 10% is to be added to Rs.70,000/- towards conventional heads.
Which comes to Rs.7,000/- Hence, the claimants are entitled for Rs.77,000/- towards conventional heads.

Considering the above facts and circumstances of the case and for the above reason,
 25 SCCH-18 MVC 3371/2023 I am of the opinion that, the petitioners are entitled for total compensation under the following heads.

Compensation heads Compensation  Amount  Towards loss of dependency Rs.20,15,000-00  Towards loss of consortium Rs. 44,000-00  Towards loss of estate Rs. 16,500-00  Towards funeral & obsequies Rs. 16,500-00  ceremony expenses  Towards transportation of Rs. 10,000-00  dead body

Accordingly, the petitioners herein are entitled to get total compensation of Rs.21,02,000/-

ISSUE NO.3:
 36.

In view of my due discussions on issue Nos.1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following;
 O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioners U/S 166 of MV Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.

The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.21,02,000/- (Rupees twenty one lakhs and two thousand only), along with the interest at the rate of 6% per annum, from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondent is liable to pay the compensation amount with interest @ 6% P.A. from the date of petition till the date of deposit to the petitioners within two months from the date of this order.

Out of the compensation amount awarded to the petitioners together with interest, the petitioner No.1 is entitled the share of 70% and the petitioner No.2 is entitled the share of 30%, out of the total award amount.

After deposit of the compensation amount together with interest, the petitioner No.1 & 2, shall deposit 40% out of their share, in any Nationalized/Scheduled bank of their choice, for a period of 3 years.
And remaining 60% shall be released to them through due process of law.

5. It is alleged in the petition that, the accident was occurred, due to the negligent act of the driver of the offending vehicle, KSRTC Bus bearing registration No.KA-19-F-3355.
In this regard, criminal case was registered against him, in Crime No.212/2023 for the offences punishable under section 279, 337 & 304(A) of IPC, on the basis of the first information, received in this regard.
As such, the respondent is liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
Hence, the petitioners have approached this court, seeking compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- consequent upon the death of G.Ravi in the alleged accident.

8. On the basis of the rival pleadings of both the parties, for final determination of this case, my  6 SCCH-18 MVC 3371/2023 predecessor in office had framed the following issues:
 *ISSUES*
 1) Whether the petitioners prove  that, G.Ravi, had died due to the  injuries sustained by him in a motor  vehicle accident that was taken  place on 18.5.2023 at about 10.00 Bhagya vs K.S.R.T.C on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99382697/
4  a.m. on Doddaballapura-Dabaspet  road, near JASS Toll, Huralihalli  cross, Bengaluru-Tumkur NH-48  road, Nelamangala, Bengaluru due  to the rash and negligent driving of  the driver of the KSRTC bus bearing  registration No.KA-19-F-3355 in an  actionable negligence?
2) Whether the petitioners are  entitled for compensation as prayed  for?
If so, at what rate?
From  whom?
3) What order or award?
As per final order,
 For the following:
 R E A S O N S  ISSUE NO.1:
 13. It is the specific case of the petitioners that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle KSRTC bus bearing registration No.KA-19-F-3355, alleged accident had taken place.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
In the said accident pillion rider by name Bhagya also, had sustained minor injuries and the deceased Ravi due to the grievous injuries, had died while taking treatment in the hospital.
As such, the rider of the two wheeler was sole responsible for the accident and its consequences.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
15. On going through the above issue, burden is on the petitioner to prove the same, by placing cogent and convincing evidence in order to find out the truth in connection with the rival contentions of both the parties with respect to the above fact in issue.
On the basis of his first information, criminal law set in motion against the driver of the KSRTC bus bearing registration No.KA-19-F-3355 alleging that, he had  11 SCCH-18 MVC 3371/2023 committed the offences punishable under section 279 and 337 of IPC.
There is no delay in giving first information about the accident.
In the recitals of Ex.P2, the complainant has clearly narrated that,
offending vehicle was coming from the back side of the defending vehicle and dashed to the two wheeler of the deceased, consequently, Ravi had succumbed to the injuries and pillion rider of the defending vehicle by name Bhagyamma also, sustained injuries in the accident.
The material documents which laid down the case against the driver of the offending vehicle, remained unquestioned and unchallenged well within time, before the competent court of law.
Further, there is no cogent evidence from the side of the respondent, to show that, due to the sole negligence on the part of the rider of the two wheeler accident in question and its consequence were taken.
Since in the death case, the legal heirs are the claimants.
On the other hand, the respondent herein, has not produced documents on record, to show the independent economic status of the petitioners, and to disprove their dependency,
with the deceased, during his life time.
By taking into consideration of all these factors, along with the evidence of PW1, it is crystal clear that, the petitioners were the dependents to the deceased during his lifetime.
 19 SCCH-18 MVC 3371/2023  26.
But in support of definite income of the deceased, there is no iota of documents to show that, the deceased was earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
In such a situation, as per law, notional income has to be taken into consideration.
Hence, the income of the deceased is apt to be taken as Rs.15,500/- p.m., which will meet the ends of justice.
The established income means the  income minus the tax component.
Having considered the above, as per law laid down in the above case, in connection with the deduction of personal and living expenses is concerned, it is settled that, "where the deceased was  22 SCCH-18 MVC 3371/2023 married, the deduction towards personal and living expenses of the deceased should be one third (1/3rd) where the number of dependent family members is 2 to 3, 1/4th where the number of Bhagya vs K.S.R.T.C on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99382697/
16 dependent family member is 4 to 6 and one fifth (1/5th ) where the number of the dependant family members exceeds six."
In the light of the above proposition, in the case on hand, 1/3rd has to be deducted towards personal and living expenses out of the total compensation.
In the present case, deceased was aged about 50 years, as on the date of the accident.
Therefore, by considering the earning of the deceased as Rs.15,500/- per month and Rs.1,86,000/- per year.
opennyai_summary.decision:
If 25% future prospects is to be taken into consideration, then it comes to Rs.2,32,500/-
(Rs.1,86,000 +Rs.46,500).
Further, 1/3rd has to be deducted towards personal and living expenses in the income of the deceased.
Which comes to Rs.20,15,000/- .
 31.
Apart from this aspect, in connection with the loss of estate, consortium, and with respect to the funeral expenses, to calculate the quantum of the compensation under the aforesaid heads, it is relevant to note herein the following authority,
 2018 SAR (Civil) 81. National Insurance Company Limited.
And  also observed that while determining the claim  petition, the reasonable figures on conventional  heads, viz., loss of estate, loss of consortium and  funeral expenses should be Rs.15,000/-,
 Rs.40,000/- and Rs.15,000/- respectively.
The  aforesaid amount should be enhanced at the rate  of 10% in every three years.
32. In the light of the proposition laid down in the aforesaid case, I am of the view that, In addition to this, the petitioner No.1 being the wife of the deceased, the petitioner No.2 & 3 being the  24 SCCH-18 MVC 3371/2023 children of the deceased, are entitled for sum of Rs.40,000/- in the head of loss of consortium.
Further, the petitioners are also entitled for sum of Rs.15,000/- towards funeral expenses.
And also the petitioners are entitled for sum of Rs.15,000/- in the head of loss to the estate.
Further the petitioners are entitled for Rs.10,000/- towards transportation of dead body.
Apart from this, it is to be noted that, in Pranay Sethi's case, the Honourable Apex court,
observed that, after expiry of every three years, from the date of judgment, 10% is to be added to Rs.70,000/- towards conventional heads.
Which comes to Rs.7,000/- Hence, the claimants are entitled for Rs.77,000/- towards conventional heads.
Considering the above facts and circumstances of the case and for the above reason,
 25 SCCH-18 MVC 3371/2023 I am of the opinion that, the petitioners are entitled for total compensation under the following heads.
Compensation heads Compensation  Amount  Towards loss of dependency Rs.20,15,000-00  Towards loss of consortium Rs. 44,000-00  Towards loss of estate Rs. 16,500-00  Towards funeral & obsequies Rs. 16,500-00  ceremony expenses  Towards transportation of Rs. 10,000-00  dead body
Accordingly, the petitioners herein are entitled to get total compensation of Rs.21,02,000/-
(Rupees twenty one lakhs and two thousand only), along with the interest at the rate of 6% per annum, as per the proposition laid down by the Honourable High court of Karnataka in MFA No.
103557/2016, Between Sri Ram General Insurance Company Limited V/S. Lakshmi And Others dated.
20.03.2018.
As such,
the respondent being the owner cum internal insurance company has to pay compensation to the petitioners, with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of the petition till its realization.
Accordingly, I am answering the issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.
In view of my due discussions on issue Nos.1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following;
 O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioners U/S 166 of MV Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.21,02,000/- (Rupees twenty one lakhs and two thousand only), along with the interest at the rate of 6% per annum, from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondent is liable to pay the compensation amount with interest @ 6% P.A. from the date of petition till the date of deposit to the petitioners within two months from the date of this order.
Out of the compensation amount awarded to the petitioners together with interest, the petitioner No.1 is entitled the share of 70% and the petitioner No.2 is entitled the share of 30%, out of the total award amount.
After deposit of the compensation amount together with interest, the petitioner No.1 & 2, shall deposit 40% out of their share, in any Nationalized/Scheduled bank of their choice, for a period of 3 years.
And remaining 60% shall be released to them through due process of law.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.500/- .
